_about: General definitions written for this project in plain words, each linked to the MedlinePlus (US National Library of Medicine) page it is based on. They describe what a test measures in general. They say nothing about any individual result and are not medical advice. Links checked 2026-11-23.

entries.title: Reference range
entries.definition: The span of results a laboratory printed for comparison, usually based on results from healthy people tested with the same method. Different labs can print different ranges for the same test, and a result just outside a range is not automatically a problem. Only a clinician who knows the person can say what a result means.

source.title: MedlinePlus: How to Understand Your Lab Results

entries.title: Units
entries.definition: The unit tells you how a result was measured, for example mg/dL (milligrams per decilitre) or mmol/L (millimoles per litre). The same test can be reported in different units, so two numbers can only be compared directly when their units match.

source.title: MedlinePlus: How to Understand Your Lab Results

entries.title: Hemoglobin A1c (HbA1c)
entries.definition: Measures how much of the hemoglobin in red blood cells has sugar attached. Because red blood cells last a few months, it reflects average blood sugar over roughly the past three months rather than a single moment.

entries.title: Glucose
entries.definition: Measures the amount of glucose (a type of sugar the body uses for energy) in the blood at the time the sample was taken. Whether the person had eaten beforehand affects the result.

entries.title: Cholesterol and triglycerides
entries.definition: A cholesterol test (often called a lipid panel) measures fats in the blood: total cholesterol, LDL cholesterol, HDL cholesterol and triglycerides. LDL and HDL are two kinds of particles that carry cholesterol around the body.

entries.title: Triglycerides
entries.definition: Triglycerides are a type of fat in the blood that the body uses to store energy. The test is usually part of a cholesterol test.

entries.title: Creatinine
entries.definition: Creatinine is a waste product made by muscles and filtered out of the blood by the kidneys. The test is one way of checking how well the kidneys are filtering.

entries.title: eGFR (estimated glomerular filtration rate)
entries.definition: An estimate of how much blood the kidneys filter each minute. It is calculated from a creatinine result together with details such as age, rather than measured directly.

entries.title: BUN (blood urea nitrogen)
entries.definition: Measures urea nitrogen, a waste product formed when the body breaks down protein, which the kidneys remove from the blood. It is often reported alongside creatinine.

entries.title: Sodium
entries.definition: Sodium is an electrolyte, a mineral that carries an electric charge in body fluids. It helps control the balance of fluid in the body and the working of nerves and muscles.

entries.title: Potassium
entries.definition: Potassium is an electrolyte that nerves and muscles, including the heart, need in order to work properly.

entries.title: Chloride
entries.definition: Chloride is an electrolyte that works with sodium and other electrolytes to keep the body's fluids and acid-base balance steady.

entries.title: Carbon dioxide (CO2, bicarbonate)
entries.definition: Measures the amount of carbon dioxide in the blood, most of it in the form of bicarbonate. It is part of the electrolyte panel and relates to the body's acid-base balance.

entries.title: Calcium
entries.definition: Measures calcium in the blood. Calcium is needed for bones and teeth and also for nerves, muscles and the heart.

entries.title: Hemoglobin
entries.definition: Hemoglobin is the protein in red blood cells that carries oxygen from the lungs to the rest of the body. It is usually measured as part of a complete blood count.

entries.title: Hematocrit
entries.definition: The percentage of the blood's volume that is made up of red blood cells.

entries.title: White blood cell count (WBC)
entries.definition: Counts the white blood cells in a sample of blood. White blood cells are part of the immune system.

entries.title: Red blood cell count (RBC)
entries.definition: Counts the red blood cells, which carry oxygen, in a sample of blood.

entries.title: MCV, MCH and MCHC
entries.definition: Measurements that describe red blood cells: MCV is their average size, MCH is the average amount of hemoglobin in each cell, and MCHC is the average concentration of hemoglobin in them. They are reported as part of a complete blood count.

entries.title: Platelet count
entries.definition: Counts platelets, small cell fragments in the blood that help it to clot.

entries.title: ALT (alanine aminotransferase)
entries.definition: ALT is an enzyme found mostly in the liver. The test measures how much of it is in the blood and is one of the liver function tests.

entries.title: AST (aspartate aminotransferase)
entries.definition: AST is an enzyme found in the liver and in other tissues such as muscle. The test measures how much is in the blood and is often reported with ALT.

entries.title: Alkaline phosphatase (ALP)
entries.definition: ALP is an enzyme found throughout the body, with much of it coming from the liver and bones. The test measures how much is in the blood.

entries.title: Bilirubin
entries.definition: Bilirubin is a yellowish substance made when the body breaks down old red blood cells. The liver processes it so it can leave the body.

entries.title: Albumin
entries.definition: Albumin is a protein made by the liver. It helps keep fluid inside blood vessels and carries substances around the body.

entries.title: Total protein
entries.definition: Measures the total amount of protein in the blood, mainly albumin and globulins.

source.title: MedlinePlus: Total Protein and Albumin/Globulin (A/G) Ratio

entries.title: Metabolic panel
entries.definition: A group of blood tests ordered together, usually including glucose, calcium, electrolytes (sodium, potassium, chloride, carbon dioxide) and kidney tests (BUN, creatinine). The comprehensive version adds liver tests and proteins.
